title: Valentine’s Day wish website with evasive “No” button and celebratory “Yes” animation

requirements.text: Create a single-page Valentine’s Day wish website that presents a playful prompt and two primary choices: a “Yes” button and an evasive “No” (or “Escape”) button.

quotes: create same code with different name
its a valentine day wish website in which multiple button option for escape and yes

acceptanceCriteria: On initial load, the page shows a Valentine’s Day themed prompt with two clear buttons: “Yes” and “No” (or “Escape”).
The experience works on both desktop and mobile screen sizes without layout breaking.

requirements.text: Implement the evasive behavior for the “No/Escape” button so that when the user attempts to click/tap it, the button moves to a new position within the visible container, making it difficult to select.

quotes: multiple button option for escape and yes

acceptanceCriteria: Attempting to click/tap “No/Escape” causes it to move to a different position within the bounds of the main content area.
The button never moves off-screen or becomes unreachable due to overflow.
The evasive behavior works with both mouse and touch interactions.

requirements.text: When the user clicks “Yes”, transition the UI into a celebration state that shows fireworks/crackers and sparkles animation and displays a Valentine’s Day message.

quotes: when click on yes its showing crackers and sparkles and. valentine day msg

acceptanceCriteria: Clicking “Yes” triggers a visible celebratory animation effect (fireworks/crackers + sparkles) lasting at least ~2 seconds.
After clicking “Yes”, a Valentine’s Day message is shown prominently on the page.
The “Yes” action cannot be accidentally re-triggered repeatedly; the UI should either disable the buttons or switch to a final state.

requirements.text: Add a simple configuration mechanism for branding text so the site name/title and the Valentine’s Day message can be changed without rewriting components (e.g., a single constants/config file used by the UI).

quotes: create same code with different name

acceptanceCriteria: There is one central place to change the displayed site name/title.
There is one central place to change the final Valentine’s Day message text.
Changing those values updates the UI on refresh without further code changes.

requirements.text: Use a coherent, creative visual theme appropriate for a Valentine’s Day wish site (consistent colors, typography, spacing, and button styling) and apply it across all UI states (initial prompt, evasive interaction, celebration state). Do not use a blue/purple theme.
acceptanceCriteria: The UI has a consistent Valentine’s Day aesthetic (e.g., warm/pink/red/cream palette, romantic typography choices, cohesive layout).
The same theme is maintained across initial and post-“Yes” celebration states.
No primary theme relies on blue/purple as the dominant palette.

requirements.text: Add required static image assets (generated) under frontend/public/assets/generated and render them in the UI as part of the visual design (do not serve images through the backend).
acceptanceCriteria: All required images listed in imageRequirements.required exist in frontend/public/assets/generated.
The UI references these images as static assets and they display correctly in the browser.
No backend code is used to fetch/serve these images.

constraints: Frontend must not modify files in the immutablePaths list: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor (no additional backend services).
Use English for any user-facing text.
nonGoals: Integrating third-party authentication providers (only Internet Identity is allowed, but not required for this app).
External database integration or non-Motoko backend services.
